name: Visual Commonsense Reasoning (VCR)
description: Visual Commonsense Reasoning (VCR) is a large-scale visual reasoning benchmark that challenges models to answer complex questions about movie scenes and provide valid natural language rationales justifying their answers ($Q \to A \to R$). Derived from 110,000 movie frames across 264,720 partitioned questions (212,923 train, 26,534 validation, and 25,263 test), answering requires commonsense knowledge about social interactions, human intent, and physical scene dynamics grounded in 800,000 object bounding boxes. These 264,720 questions give rise to 290,000 multiple-choice problems across answer prediction ($Q \to A$) and rationale justification ($QA \to R$).
